entrant_id.description: Stable id. Must equal the file name without .json. Forecast files use this id.

organization.description: Company or research group behind the entry. Public, shown next to the display name.

type.description: `participant` is any outside entrant answering from its own endpoint; the site's registration form writes it. The other values are the arena's own entries.

method.description: One or two sentences: what generates the forecasts. Written for the arena's own entries; a participant may leave it out.

arms.description: For LLM entrants: information-access arms you will submit under. 'closed' is the question plus the series history and nothing else; 'news' adds the arena's fixed, archived news digest, identical for every entrant and frozen at the lock; 'web' is live search, which is why it is prospective-only -- in a backtest the outcome is already published.

status.description: Absent means active, so no existing registration changes meaning. 'revoked' is the off switch for both routes at once: the bundle intake refuses an upload before issuing a receipt, and tools/probe_agent_api.py refuses to call the endpoint. It is recorded here rather than only in a private console because a participant has to be able to see, from the public record, that the arena has stopped reaching them -- a revocation nobody can observe is indistinguishable from an outage.

contact.description: Contact email, optional. Public in this file; leave it out to be reached through the `github` account instead.

github.description: GitHub login of the person or organisation that registered this entrant. CI refuses a pull request that edits this file, or files forecasts under this entrant id, unless its author is this account or a maintainer (tools/validate_submission.py --author). Required for registrations opened by pull request since 2026-09-05; older hand-written registrations without it are maintained by the maintainers.

route.description: Route A only: where the arena calls this entrant. Absent means the entrant hands forecasts over itself (a pull request with forecast files), which is what every registration written before this field did -- so absent has to keep meaning exactly that. There is no credential anywhere in this block and there will not be one: the arena signs every request it sends (ssa/signing.py, public key in site/keys.json) and the participant verifies. A block that could name a credential could name ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

kind.description: The only route kind. Named rather than implied so a second one is an added value here, not a guess about a missing field.

url.description: The exact HTTPS URL the arena POSTs each question to, as one JSON object; the reply body is the forecast, one JSON object. Plain http is refused here and again in code: the signature says who sent the request, https is what keeps a third party from reading the question or rewriting the reply in transit. No query string or fragment, so a URL cannot smuggle a credential.
